segments.narration: Two percent of this town hear a noise nobody else can. Same room, same moment, and only some people register it.
They describe a low droning, like a distant idling truck that never drives away. It drives people out of their bedrooms.
segments.visual_query: quiet adobe house night new mexico

segments.narration: Measured reports land between 32 and 80 hertz, slowly pulsing. The bottom edge of what a human ear does.
A 1973 study of fifty cases found something odd. Cool weather, light breeze, early morning, and confined to a ten-kilometre patch.
The leading explanation is not outside at all. Low-frequency tinnitus and the ear's own emissions can generate it, in a very quiet town.
